title: Exact Security of TNT-SM4-32
summary: A known distinguisher does not directly apply to TNT-SM4-32’s 32-bit tweak space but breaks a prior beyond-the-birthday-bound proof; its exact security and BBB status remain open.

formal_statement.body: For $\mathrm{TNT\text{-}SM4\text{-}32}$, the tweak space is limited to $32$ bits. A known distinguisher requires $O(2^{n/2})$ tweaks with $n=128$ and therefore does not directly apply to $\mathrm{TNT\text{-}SM4\text{-}32}$, although it breaks a prior beyond-the-birthday-bound security proof. Determine the exact security of $\mathrm{TNT\text{-}SM4\text{-}32}$ and whether it achieves beyond-the-birthday-bound security despite its restricted tweak space.

scope.domain: Security analysis of the restricted-tweak TNT-SM4-32 block-cipher construction.
parameters: 32-bit tweak space: the restricted tweak domain of TNT-SM4-32
n = 128: the parameter governing the known distinguisher's tweak requirement
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine the exact security of TNT-SM4-32 and whether it achieves beyond-the-birthday-bound security with its restricted tweak space.

citations.label: Tight Security of TNT and Beyond: Attacks, Proofs and Possibilities for the Cascaded LRW Paradigm

progress.summary: The source says its distinguisher does not directly apply because TNT-SM4-32’s tweak space is too small, yet it breaks a prior beyond-the-birthday-bound security proof. It explicitly leaves the construction’s exact security and beyond-the-birthday-bound status open.
